items.author: main session (sprint 58 military design, 2026-10-26)
items.title: Seven land classes by equipment generation, and their equipment as goods
items.design: MILITARY.md § Land — the classes. Infantry, motorised, mechanised, armour, light armour, artillery, air defence; each a class x equipment generation with soft, hard, hardness, defence, breakthrough. Equipment goods (small arms, armoured vehicles and artillery pieces by generation, air defence systems, drones) with recipes; hire buys the class's kit off the shelf. FPV drones are equipment raising soft/hard attack. Tech gates generations (DIGITISATION_TREE ST-FO). The campaign roster table is the class table; the Era -1 nineteen rows are untouched.

items.author: main session (sprint 58 military design, 2026-10-26)
items.title: Wounded units refit from the shelf; spent units retreat; readiness recovers out of contact
items.design: MILITARY.md § Land — equipment, refit and manpower. Each tick a unit below full HP draws equipment and manpower to regain HP; unmet draws leave it wounded. A unit at readiness 0 moves one tile away from the enemy (a legal march, deterministic tile pick). Readiness recovers out of contact, capped by morale. Morale is per unit, moved by supply, victories, losses and war exhaustion. Conservation: men and goods drawn equal HP regained.

items.author: main session (sprint 58 military design, 2026-10-26)
items.title: Soldiers are drawn from the nation's labour pool, conscript or professional
items.design: MILITARY.md § Land — equipment, refit and manpower; POPULATION.md § The labour pool. A unit's men are labour taken from the (nation, body) pool before buildings staff, so mobilisation empties factories. A national choice between conscript (cheap per head, wide labour drain, lower quality) and professional (wages, fewer, better). Measure the labour effect on market_viability before tuning.

items.author: main session (sprint 58 military design, 2026-10-26)
items.title: A war has a score, exhaustion, and a peace: white, ceded, or imposed at 100; then a truce
items.design: RELATIONS.md § 7 (Ben, 2026-10-30: the full war, not declaration only). War score -100..100 from occupation of goals (province_holder, tile-weighted) and battle strength destroyed, half each; exhaustion 0-100 per party from strength lost, days in the field and provinces held by the enemy, decaying at peace, moving unit morale (MILITARY.md stats table). Peace offers in their own table, one pending per war: white peace or cession of held goals; impose at 100; both hostility rows clear; the record closes to history; a sixteen-tick truce bars re-declaration. Cession's territorial half is BL-1460 (cession moves territory). Declaration and the record are BL-1459.

items.author: main session
items.title: Fronts: a neighbour with no free key tile has no front; unreachable front marches retry every tick
items.design: Two edge cases from the BL-1427 (fronts) cold review. (1) Keys are unique per nation and claimed smallest span first, so a span whose every tile another front already claimed has no key and is dropped: a nation touching B only at one tile it also shares with A has no front toward B, against "Every neighbour has fronts" (MILITARY.md § Fronts). 0 cases on the generated world; fronts_harness F1g fails if a seed hits one. Fix by naming a front by (neighbour, tile) or a tie rule that never leaves a span unnamed. (2) A front march the game refuses (the slot or push target on another landmass) is re-issued every tick, re-pathing the province each time; the rival scorer assigns idle units with no reachability check. Assign only to fronts the unit can reach, or stop re-issuing a refused march.

items.author: main session (cold review of BL-1434/BL-1446)
items.title: Hire and refit check goods by price as well as quantity; the PNG inflate gets an output cap
items.design: Cold review of unit designs, 2026-10-28. (1) HIGH, latent until later kit unlocks (BL-1436): hire_goods_affordable counts shelf quantity only, while buy_from_corp_shelves charges the posted price capped by purse_room_of, and debit_kit_goods ignores how much it bought. A design refit (0 credits) with a committed treasury gets its kit free; a hire at exact room drops the treasury below its commitments. The row-goods leg had the flaw already. Fix: the affordability check sums qty x posted price plus the credit cost against purse_room_of, and apply asserts the bought amount. (2) LOW: hire_goods_affordable prices each row axis at its first candidate without the kit draw on the same resource, so an affordable hire can be refused. (3) LOW: png_decode.cpp inflate has no output cap; stop once out exceeds h x (stride+1). (4) LOW: the refit menu labels a design refit with the row gate (+ kit) and omits the changed slots goods; an obsolete own row moves the (live design) entry to the end.

items.author: main session (sprint 61 diplomacy design, 2026-10-30)
items.title: A war is a record: declare_war with goals, a priced declaration, justifications, the free answer
items.design: RELATIONS.md § 7 (Ben, 2026-10-30). The war record per (declarer, defender) on world and in the snapshot (save version bump). declare_war(declarer, defender, goals) writes hostility and the record atomically; refused with nothing mutated on an existing war, a truce or an invalid goal (1-3 of the defender's provinces, any of them, capitals included). Justifications as condition_set rows (grievance, embargo, lost ground, a friend attacked) halving the war_declared price; a price preview read for the ledger. items.author: main session (sprint 61 diplomacy design, 2026-10-30)
items.title: A peace that cedes moves tile_to_nation; a white peace hands occupied goals back
items.design: RELATIONS.md § 7, Cession moves the territory (Ben, 2026-10-30); MILITARY.md § Battles, the holder paragraph. For each ceded province tile_to_nation follows province_holder: buildings change owner with the ground, the population centre, law jurisdiction, road network membership, and fronts re-derive; the loser's units on ceded ground withdraw by the retreat rule. A white peace resets every occupied goal's holder to its owner and withdraws the occupiers. The heaviest seam in the sprint: check money_conservation, fold_census, save_roundtrip, world_determinism and the front harnesses, plus a cession_harness that cedes on a library seed and walks every consumer of tile_to_nation. File names are a guess; read the code first. A ceded capital moves to the largest remaining population centre with its free hub; a peace that would cede a nation's last province is refused (Ben, 2026-10-30, NR-1102).

items.author: main session (sprint 61 diplomacy design, 2026-10-30)
items.title: A rival nation wages war: declares with goals, answers, makes and imposes peace
items.design: RELATIONS.md § 1 Who declares and § 7 (Ben, 2026-10-30: the 2026-08-18 stance grant covers a rival declaring war). The scorer reads its own sentiment and Alarm toward a nation, the price and justifications, front strength and trade exposure; it declares via declare_war only, never on a threshold alone, and never as a planner. Pure, seeded, deterministic, replayable. Answering, offering, accepting, refusing and imposing peace are granted on the same terms (Ben, 2026-10-30, NR-1100; AI_OPPONENT.md § 11, "Rival nations wage war whole"), so a peace it scores may cede ground. The player's nation is never scored. Check: stance_determinism, spectator_determinism, a war-count band across the 16 library seeds (no world where every nation is at war by tick 40, none where none ever is).
